messages.subject: Not able to use rhread inside map expression
parts:
Hi,

I have an lapply which I want to implement using map on hadoop(as
lapply is taking too much time on local machine, big dataset being the
reason). Tried using rhlapply but came across an earlier post on this
group that it has been removed and the following was suggested:

"Sorry about the out -of -sync landing page.
rhlapply and rhwordcount have been removed.
rhlapply can be implemented like this
rhlapply(N, F) #apply F to 1..N
map = expression({
lapply(map.values, function(r) {
rhcollect(r, F(r))
})
})

rhmr(map, inout=c("lapply","seq"), N=N)
Should work "


Tried to follow this. Used seq_along(x) ('x' is an object I created
earlier) instead of map.values and got the error that object 'x'
cannot be found(while running rhex). Why is this?

Next I tried to solve this by creating 'x' inside the map expression
itself by:

x = rhread(blah blah blah)

and got the error that 'function rhread cannot be found' once again
during rhex !!!!!!!!!!
Now tell me when rhcollect() can be found inside the map expression y
the hell can rhread() not be found?????

And lastly (and of lesser importance) in rhmr my N is equal to
length(seq_along(x)), but if i do my 'x=rhread(blah blah blah)' (if
that can be done) inside the map expression, how can i access that
value in my rhmr for N?

Hope u have understood my problem and please suggest a solution to
this.

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Not able to use rhread inside map expression
parts:
>
> Tried to follow this. Used seq_along(x) ('x' is an object I created
> earlier) instead of map.values and got the error that object 'x'
> cannot be found(while running rhex). Why is this?

Objects you create in the R environment won't be passed to the map expression.
when inout[1] is 'lapply', map.values contains integers 1 ... N where
N is specified in rhmr.

You can manually use rhwrite to write your list to disk and then
inout=c("seq",'seq") and the rhwite output
can be your input.

>
> Next I tried to solve this by creating 'x' inside the map expression
> itself by:
>
> x = rhread(blah blah blah)
>
> and got the error that 'function rhread cannot be found' once again

You cannot use rhread inside the map expression. The documentation
says what functions are available to the rhipe user
in the map and reduce expression: rhcollect, rhstatus and rhcounter.

> during rhex !!!!!!!!!!

No need to get excited.

> Now tell me when rhcollect() can be found inside the map expression y
> the hell can rhread() not be found?????

Relax. Reserve your frustration. Why the hell
1. Do book publishers have greedy control over ebooks?
2. Google becoming the gateway to the worlds books?
3. prop 8 was voted yes in California?
4. can the US not provide health care to all?
and many more ...

rhread is designed to read from the HDFS. In the mapreduce code, I
have no intention of allowing the user reading from the HDFS.
You can share datasets using the shared parameter which copies the
HDFS backed data to the local side.

> And lastly (and of lesser importance) in rhmr my N is equal to
> length(seq_along(x)),  but if i do my 'x=rhread(blah blah blah)' (if
> that can be done) inside the map expression, how can i access that
> value in my rhmr for N?
>

Because it's not available. Use inout=c("seq","seq"), write your list
objectusing rhwrite and use that folder
as an ifolder.

Cheers
Saptarshi

If you're trying to convert your data frame to some input ready for
RHIPE in the way you need it, you in for some problems
.

(Quick digression) if you're using data frames in RHIPE, try and set
stringsAsFactors=FALSE, factors take extra space.

1. A data frame is a list. Each column is a list entry. If you write
the data frame using rhwrite, and the rhread it again. You get (what
you saw):

x <- data.frame(Shape=c("Cuboid","Cube","Pyramid"),Length=c(5,5,4),Breadth=c(6,5,4),
Height=c(7,5,7),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
rhwrite(x,"/wsc/tmp/myx",N=2)

> rhread('/wsc/tmp/myx/1')
RHIPE: Read 2 pairs occupying 81 bytes, deserializing
[[1]]
[[1]][[1]]
[1] "Breadth"

[[1]][[2]]
[1] 6 5 4


[[2]]
[[2]][[1]]
[1] "Height"

[[2]][[2]]
[1] 7 5 7

Each column is key-value pair. The key is the column name, the value
is the column.

You want to convert this into {Cuboid, (5,6,7) }, {Cube, (5,5,5)}.

1. Now if your data frame (8GB) is massive, you're not going to read
into R, right?
Why not write the input schema (which i guess is on disk) in this email?

If, on disk, it looks like
And you want an output of the form

You could do

rows.of.lines <- strsplit(unlist(map.values)," ")
shape <- unlist(lapply(rows.lines,"[[",1))
lengths <- as.numeric(unlist(lapply(rows.lines,"[[",2))
breadth <- as.numeric(unlist(lapply(rows.lines,"[[",3))
height <- as.numeric(unlist(lapply(rows.lines,"[[",3))

for(i in seq_along(rows.of.lines))
rhcollect(shape[[i]], c(lengths[[i]],breadth[[i]], height[[i]]))

Your data set is now key-value of the shape you desire.

Have I understood you wrong? Do you actually have an 8GB data frame in memory?
if that is the case, then write it to disk, (stripping of row.names
and column.names), save it to the HDFS
and use inout[1] = 'text' and do as I described above.


hope it helps
Saptarshi

parts:
Recommend you think only about accomplishing one task in one
MapReduce.

As far as processing large text csv files that scales nicely, but you
do have to split the csv line yourself. There is an example of this
in your documentation. The end result gets you to R objects.

Then a new map reduce you process the R objects.

Is this example consistent in the sense that every vector row always
has the same length?

Shape
Cuboid Cube Pyramid
Length
5 5 4
Breadth
6 5 4
Height
7 5 7

You could key the value by index of the vector in the map and let
hadoop collect them together in the sort/shuffle.

Eg
If at the start of the map keys are Shape, Length, Breadth, Height and
values are c(Cuboid, Cube, Pyramid), c(5,5,4), c(6,5,4), c(7,5,7)

Then a map reduce is
map = expression({

})
